get.description:
How much cash the household needs over the window, and how much above that could be invested: `surplus` is `cash_available` minus `cash_needed`, and `cash_needed` is the planned outflows, plus the goals, plus the safety floor, minus any income counted.

`status` says how far to trust it. `firm` is a number with nothing to warn about. `provisional` is a number with `cautions`, each saying what might change it. `unavailable` is no number: `surplus` is `null` and `blockers` say why, such as a safety floor not yet set or an account without a balance. Several currencies are never netted: `surplus` is `null`, with the blocker `mixed_currencies`, and each row of `totals` has its own.

A planned amount is a positive magnitude with a `direction`. Balances, `cash_available`, `projected_cash` and `surplus` carry a sign: a card owing money is negative, and a negative `surplus` is a shortfall. Amounts are integer minor units.

A bill or one-off a person settled for a month (`settlePlanItem`) counts as nothing in that month: no gross, no gap, no caution, no share of its category's spending. `settled` lists it with its amount, so no number silently differs, and it doesn't make the status `provisional` of itself, since a person decided.

Every number traces to its lines: `accounts` says which balances counted, `items` what each planned item added, `months` the same by calendar month. A stored budget counts its whole month: its occurrences earlier in `as_of`'s month are on its line and in the first month, less the spending bills and one-offs dated up to `as_of` leave in its category. This month's spending counts only where a balance already shows it: posted, not pending, on or before its account's balance date, and not removed or revised by its provider, though a refund flagged so still counts. Money out a balance may not show raises the caution `spending_newer_than_balance`, with `total` for what posted after the balance's date and `pending` for what has not posted, and leaves the number as it is: the forecast assumes each balance already reflects them, so where one doesn't, the cash available is overstated by up to those amounts. Only `expense` spending lowers what a goal needs, so moving money to savings for a goal doesn't.

Needs `read`; a token with account grants also needs `all` at `transactions`, since the answer sums every account. The refusal is the same whatever exists.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description:
The first day of the window, written exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the years 1970 to
2200: by default the household's today. A balance is the latest on or before
it. Any other day than today raises the caution `as_of_not_today`, since what
falls due before that day's month is left out, as is planned income dated on or
before that day and any hypothetical item dated before it. Planned income counts
only from the day after it, today or not, since a balance of that day may already
hold that day's money.

parameters.name: horizon_months
parameters.description: How many months the window covers, by default the household's setting.

parameters.description:
Whether planned inflows reduce the cash needed, by default the household's

post.description: Creates a recurring item, a one-off or a goal (a sinking fund). An outflow needs an `expense` category and an inflow an `income` one; a goal must be an outflow. A recurring outflow is a `bill`, counted in full, unless `spending` makes it a `budget`, which counts all of this month's occurrences, those already past too, less what was spent in its category so far this month; nothing else takes `spending`. A goal and a one-off describing the same expense are both counted, so the expense counts twice: nothing de-duplicates them. Its type never changes once it exists. Needs `write`; a token with account grants also needs `all` at `write`. With an `Idempotency-Key`, a retry of the same request within 24 hours returns the first response instead of creating again.

get.description:
What the household is worth, period by period, in the display currency.

A point is the value on the last day of its period, or on the last day available when it says `partial`: `on` is that day and `period_start` the first day of the period inside the range. A week ends on Sunday. Each account's latest balance on or before `on` counts, so a balance carries forward until a newer one. A period where nothing counts is left out, and at most 1,000 periods are answered: a longer range is 422, whatever is stored. `through` is the last day with values: no later day, and no day after today, is a point.

`total` is the sum of the counted accounts' amounts, each converted and rounded on its own, so every breakdown adds up to it. It is `null`, never a partial sum, when one of them has no amount: `unconverted` names the accounts, and a caution says why. A `by_liquidity` line is `null` the same way. `by_currency` is the native sum per currency, with no rate involved, so nothing is omitted; only an account with no value that day can't be in it.

In `accounts`, each account says whether it counts, its `first_on` (a jump that day is an account arriving, not money) and its `closed_on` (a closed account stops counting that day unless it still owes). Its `points` say the `balance` in its own currency, `balance_on`, the date of the snapshot that balance comes from, `balance_source`, the `amount` in the display currency and `rate_on`, the older of the dates of the rates used: a weekend reports Friday's.

`status` says how far to trust it. `firm` is numbers with nothing to warn about. `provisional` is numbers with `cautions`. `unavailable` is `blockers`: `display_currency_not_set` (an admin has to choose one, and points still hold `by_currency`), `rebuilding` (no points until the values are rebuilt) or `no_counted_accounts` (not a net worth of zero).

The cautions: `rate_missing`, with a reason of `not_fetched_yet`, `not_published`, `fetch_failing`, `provider_off` or `none_that_early`; `rate_stale`, a rate more than a week older than its day, as for a discontinued currency; `amount_too_large`, a conversion that doesn't fit; `balance_stale`, an old balance on the latest point; `to_date_not_yet_filled`, later days not answered yet; `daily_value_missing`, an account with no value on a day after its first, which is a hole and not money leaving; `nothing_counted_after_last_point`, so the last point isn't the value now; `liability_balance_positive`, perhaps a wrong sign, added as it stands; and `closed_account_owing`, a debt still counting.

Needs `read`. **A token with account grants gets the sum of the accounts it can see at `balances`, and nothing marks it as partial**, since that would reveal that there are others. An agent holding such a token must not report the sum as the whole household's. Nothing in the answer depends on an account the token can't see, except that rates are stored once for the household: a currency the token sees has its rates as soon as anyone's use fetched them. Amounts are integer minor units. It writes nothing.

get.description:
Per category and month, what the plan says against what happened. `planned` is the occurrences of today's active items falling in the month, not spread across months, and the plan has no history, so changing an item rewrites past months. `actual` is posted splits on any account: positive for spending in an `expense` category and for income in an `income` one, net of refunds, so it can be negative. `transfer` categories don't count. `difference` is `planned` minus `actual`, and `rolling_average` the mean of `actual` over the `average_months` calendar months ending at that month, zeros included.

Money that isn't in `actual` is still reported, at what its splits say, not the transaction's revised amount. A charge, or a deposit in an `income` category, whose provider removed it or revised it away from its splits stays out of `actual`, with the amount in `left_out`; a refund on such a transaction keeps counting. A possible duplicate stays in `actual`, with the amount in `possible_duplicate`. A split linked to a goal counts only on that goal's line in `goals`, as `spent_against` beside what its schedule `accrued`, and a removed, revised or possibly duplicate charge there is in that line's `left_out`. Outflows with no splits are never spending: `uncategorized` lists them, without invested and illiquid accounts.

An occurrence a person settled (`settlePlanItem`) stays in `planned`, since it is what was planned: a row's `settled` says how much of `planned` it is, and the list `settled` says which item, for which month, and whether `paid` or `skipped`. A settled occurrence takes no share of the spending in `rollovers`, since that spending wasn't for it.

`rollovers` has a line for each category and currency with a budget: what was `budgeted` over the reported months up to today's, what they `spent` on it while a budget was running, once bills and one-offs dated up to today have taken their share, and the `rollover` between them, positive for unspent and negative for overspent. It is a window over those months, not a running balance, so moving `from` changes it, and today's month counts all its budget occurrences. A bill has none, and the forecast doesn't carry it over. `partial_months` names the reported month holding today, whose figures aren't final. Amounts are integer minor units, and currencies are never netted.

Needs `read`; a token with account grants also needs `all` at `transactions`, since the answer sums every account. The refusal is the same whatever exists.

spending so far. The gap counts as still needed; if it was paid under another

anyway, since overstating the need is the safe direction.

Possible duplicates this month might be inflating a category's spending, which
could shrink a reduction or hide an unpaid bill or one-off.

date. A transaction is one or the other. The number stays as it is, since a
provider's balance date may lag what its balance reflects, and guessing could
count the money twice or not at all. Where a balance doesn't show it, the cash

Between these points a currency's rate was missing, so amounts in it are
`null`.
The point at which an amount used the oldest rate, older than a week.

`null`.
On the latest point, this counted balance dates from `on`.

The last filled day is before the end of the range, or today if that is
earlier: later dates are not answered yet.

Between these points an account already holding values has none, so what
holds it is `null`, it is in `unconverted`, and its balance is in no

last point is older than the range's end and is not the value now: every

was added as it stands. `balance` is from the last point where it did.
